Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: First pass registers one primary, falsifiable dependency hypothesis for most dependency endpoints, plus one subgroup interaction. The strongest prior directions are oncogene addiction or known synthetic-lethal relationships: BRAF V600E for BRAF; EGFR or ERBB2 amplification for EGFR/ERBB2; KRAS mutation for KRAS, with an interaction hypothesis that KRAS dependency is stronger in lung adenocarcinoma than in the complement; MSI-high for WRN; SWI/SNF loss (SMARCA4 or ARID1A) for SMARCA2; KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2; MYC amplification for transcriptional/translation/replication-stress dependencies POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9; ERBB2 amplification for TMED10 trafficking dependency; RB1 loss for KIF18A spindle/aneuploidy dependency; and PTEN loss for STAT3 signaling dependency. For MDM2 and USP7, I expect TP53 loss to reduce dependency, i.e., the dependency score becomes less negative, so the raw TP53-loss minus TP53-nonloss contrast is positive and direction=+1. For RIT1, I tentatively expect KRAS mutation to reduce dependency because KRAS may bypass RIT1-mediated RAS activation, also direction=+1. Direction=+1 therefore denotes an exposed group with a higher/less-negative score; direction=-1 denotes a more negative/stronger dependency score. I will interpret results as scientifically meaningful only if the signed mean_difference is in the claimed direction, the 95% interval excludes zero, and the absolute difference is around at least 0.02-0.03, approximately the 10% magnitude scale for many negative dependency scores. These are associations in the supplied lung cancer cell-line dataset and not causal or generalizable claims until further uncertainty and independent validation are considered.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery evidence. For dependency scores that are mostly negative and centered around roughly -0.25, I treated an absolute difference of about 0.025-0.03 as approximately the 10% clinically meaningful scale, while also considering the interval bounds. Three claims show extremely large, direction-consistent effects: MSI-high versus non-MSI cells have much stronger WRN dependency (H6/R5), TP53 loss versus no TP53 loss has much weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency (H8/R7), and SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss has much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H9/R8). These effects are far outside the 10%-scale threshold and their intervals do not approach zero. Multiplicity across 12 tests is negligible for effects of this size, so I accept them as scientifically meaningful associations within this supplied dataset. These are still not causal or generalizable claims; co-mutation structure, lineage subtype, library/batch, screen quality, and culture covariates could in principle contribute, and I have not adjusted for them. H11 is a large and precise effect but in the opposite direction of the registered claim. Because the estimate is signed to direction -1, the reported -0.796 corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast of approximately +0.796, i.e., KEAP1-loss cells have much less negative/ weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I therefore reject the original stronger-NFE2L2-dependency hypothesis rather than reinterpret it post hoc. H2 is the only borderline claim that warrants validation: the signed effect is about +0.025, around the 10% scale, with an interval from approximately -0.00025 to +0.0507. This is consistent with the hypothesized direction but not decisive under multiplicity, so I request independent validation. The other claims are small, interval-inclusive of zero, and either non-informative or only weakly suggestive. I keep H4 deferred because the KRAS lineage-subtype interaction H5 may be more informative than the overall KRAS main effect; I close the remaining low-priority nulls to concentrate validation and follow-up on stronger or more ambiguous signals.

prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Validation resolves H2 against the original claim. H2 asked whether EGFR-amplified cells have stronger dependency_EGFR, i.e. a more negative score. Because the claim direction is -1, positive signed estimates represent the hypothesized stronger dependency and negative signed estimates represent the opposite. Discovery R2 gave a borderline signed effect of about +0.025, roughly at the 10%-scale threshold for these scores, with an interval from essentially zero to +0.051; it was not decisive. Independent validation R13 gave the opposite signed effect, about -0.028, with an adjusted interval from -0.071 to +0.014. The validation point estimate is negative and its upper bound is below the 0.025 magnitude scale, so a clinically meaningful EGFR-amplification-associated stronger EGFR dependency is not supported. Together, discovery and validation are inconsistent and do not establish a meaningful dataset association; I therefore reject H2 and close it. This is a conclusion about the supplied data, not proof that EGFR amplification is unrelated to EGFR dependency in other datasets or causal contexts. The supported dataset-level findings remain H6, H8, and H9: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency, TP53-loss cells have much weaker/less-negative USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. These have signed effects near 0.78-0.80, far above the 10% threshold and far outside zero; they are associations, not causal or generalizable claims. H11 remains rejected because the observed KEAP1-loss effect on NFE2L2 is large and opposite to the original direction; I have registered the reversed direction as a new unresolved hypothesis rather than reinterpreting H11 post hoc. Negative or non-supporting main-effect evidence remains small or interval-inclusive for H1, H3, H7, H14, H16, and H18, and H4 remains deferred pending the KRAS lineage-subtype interaction H5. The most informative next analyses are to evaluate the already registered unevaluated claims H5, H10, H12, H13, H15, and H17, plus the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 proposal. If any new result is near the 0.025 threshold, validation should be used before acceptance; otherwise validation resources can be conserved for genuinely borderline discoveries.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

expectation

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: This corrected explore-stage submission adds focused, falsifiable dataset-level hypotheses after the prior evidence and avoids refinement proposals without available motivating evidence. No discovery assessments were due, but H19 already has direct discovery evidence R9 for the reversed KEAP1-loss direction. Because R9 gives a very large positive signed difference for direction +1, it indicates that KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker/less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 than KEAP1-intact cells. This is far above the approximate 10% absolute scale for these scores and the interval excludes zero, so I accept H19 as a supported association within this supplied dataset and close it. I do not infer causality or generalizability. For new comparisons, I registered refinements linked to available evidence where appropriate: ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells for SMARCA2 dependency, motivated by the accepted SMARCA4-loss synthetic-lethal signal; CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for MDM2 dependency, motivated by the weak but registered TP53-loss MDM2 hypothesis; and MYC amplification among TP53-intact cells for DHX9 dependency, motivated by the prior MYC-DHX9 test. I also added direct biologically motivated contrasts: TP53 loss on RPL11 because RPL11 participates in p53/ribosomal-stress signaling, ERBB2 amplification on STAT3 as an alternative signaling driver to PTEN loss, and MYC amplification on KIF18A as a mitotic/replication-stress hypothesis. For all, acceptance will require signed direction, 95% Welch interval separation from zero, and an effect size near or above the approximate 10% magnitude scale for the relevant dependency score; borderline results will merit validation before acceptance.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered discovery evidence using the signed intervals as reported and interpreted clinically meaningful effects by comparing them to an outcome-specific 10% scale, roughly 0.025 for most dependency scores near -0.25, about 0.04 for SMARCA2, and smaller for NFE2L2/USP7. H17 is the clearest new positive finding: PTEN loss versus no PTEN loss gives a signed difference of +0.267 (95% interval +0.215 to +0.319) for dependency_STAT3 under direction -1. This corresponds to a raw contrast of about -0.27, i.e. PTEN-loss cells have much stronger STAT3 dependency. The lower bound is far above the STAT3 10% scale and multiplicity across 12 tests is not a concern for an effect this large, so I accept it as a supported association within this dataset. I reject H21 because, among TP53-intact cells, CDKN2A loss versus intact gives a large negative signed effect for a +1 direction (+1 direction here means positive raw contrast, i.e. weaker dependency), with interval entirely on the opposite side of zero and far beyond the MDM2 threshold. The data instead suggest CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, so I reject the original direction and register a reversed new proposal linked to H21. H5 shows no meaningful KRAS-mutation interaction with adenocarcinoma subtype: the signed interaction is near zero and in the wrong direction, with an interval crossing zero; I close it as unresolved because it is not informative enough to establish absence. H10 and H20 test ARID1A loss against SMARCA2 dependency overall and in SMARCA4-intact cells. Both intervals have positive signed upper bounds well below the much larger SMARCA2 10% scale, and point estimates are opposite or null, so I reject claims of clinically meaningful stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H13 rejects MYC amplification as associated with clinically meaningful stronger RPL11 dependency; the positive signed interval is small and its upper bound is below threshold. H22 similarly rejects a clinically meaningful TP53-loss effect on RPL11 in the registered +1 direction: the effect is tiny and the interval is mostly within the 10% band. H12 remains unresolved but closed because the interval upper bound is very near the POLR2A threshold while the point estimate is negligible; it is too imprecise for a negative conclusion and too small for acceptance. H15, H24, and H25 are low-priority unresolved nulls or imprecise small effects; their upper bounds can reach threshold but point estimates are not near enough to justify validation now. H23 is borderline: ERBB2 amplification shows a signed +0.022 effect on STAT3, just below the STAT3 threshold with a wide interval that includes both null and clinically meaningful values. I defer it rather than accept, but it is a reasonable future validation target. I request validation for H4 rather than H23 now because H4 is a central matched KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency effect with larger exposed-group sample size and more stable variance; independent validation can more efficiently resolve whether the main effect reaches the 10% scale after the lineage-subtype interaction H5 was uninformative. None of these conclusions should be read as causal or generalizable; they remain dataset-level associations that could be influenced by co-mutation structure, lineage subtype, batch/library, screen quality, culture covariates, or unmeasured dependencies.

Study instructions:

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

record.narrative: New validation resolves H4 against the original KRAS-dependency claim. H4 was registered in the direction stronger dependency in KRAS-mutant cells; therefore positive signed estimates mean exposed-minus-comparator dependency_KRAS is more negative. Discovery R4 was only borderline positive, about +0.014, with a 95% Welch interval from -0.004 to +0.031 and a point estimate below the roughly 0.025 clinical-scale threshold for these scores. Independent validation R26 was essentially null and opposite, about -0.001, with an independent interval from -0.026 to +0.025. The discovery and validation evidence are inconsistent, and the validation upper bound is at or below the approximate 10% scale, so I reject H4 and close the investigation. This is a conclusion about the supplied data and not proof that KRAS mutation cannot affect KRAS dependency in other settings. H2 remains rejected for the analogous reason: EGFR amplification did not show a supported clinically meaningful stronger EGFR dependency, and validation was opposite to the original direction. I also accept H26 as a strong dataset-level association: among TP53-intact cells, CDKN2A loss is associated with substantially stronger MDM2 dependency, with signed effect about +0.119 and a 95% interval from +0.079 to +0.158, far above the relevant threshold. This is an association in the supplied dataset, not causal evidence and not necessarily generalizable. record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due at this explore stage. I propose focused, falsifiable dataset-level comparisons that either test new pathway predictors for dependencies not explained by accepted markers or refine accepted effects by checking specificity/robustness. First, PIK3CA activating mutation versus STAT3 dependency tests whether PI3K/AKT pathway activation associates with stronger STAT3 dependence; the alternative is null or opposite because STAT3 is already associated with PTEN loss and the dataset could reflect co-mutation structure. Second, NF1 loss versus KRAS dependency tests a RAS-GAP loss prediction, which may be more informative than KRAS mutation status after H4 failed. Third, ERBB2 amplification versus RIT1 dependency tests downstream RAS-pathway activation; ERBB2 STAT3 is already under active testing, but RIT1 gives an alternative signaling-node hypothesis. Fourth, KRAS mutation versus BRAF dependency tests whether upstream RAS activation increases dependence on downstream RAF. Fifth, MYC amplification is refined to cells with high MYC transcript abundance for POLR2A dependency, because amplification status alone may be an incomplete exposure; H12 was unresolved and imprecise. Sixth, the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 synthetic-lethal association is tested for effect modification by ARID1A loss, hypothesizing stronger SMARCA2 dependency when both alternative BAF targeting subunits are lost. Seventh, the accepted MSI-high/WRN association is restricted to TP53-intact cells to test whether the large effect is robust to p53-pathway co-occurrence. All proposals are scored as dataset associations; acceptance would require signed effect directions consistent with biology, intervals excluding zero, and magnitudes approaching the outcome-specific approximately 10% clinically meaningful scale. None should be read as causal or generally generalizable.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I audited the new discovery results using the signed intervals as supplied and the approximate 10% clinically meaningful dependency scale used earlier: about 0.028 for STAT3, 0.024-0.026 for most dependency scores near a mean of -0.25, about 0.030 for WRN, and about 0.041 for SMARCA2. More negative dependency values mean stronger dependency; for a direction of -1, positive signed estimates therefore mean stronger dependency in the exposed group. H27 is the only clinically interesting but borderline new result. ERBB2 amplification among PTEN-intact cells gives a signed STAT3 difference of +0.032 (95% Welch interval +0.003 to +0.060), which exceeds the approximate 0.028 threshold at the point estimate and is directionally consistent with the idea that ERBB2 signaling may increase STAT3 dependence. However, the lower confidence limit is well below the clinically meaningful threshold, the exposed stratum contains only 145 amplified lines, and the result could be influenced by co-amplification or lineage structure. It is therefore not strong enough to accept without confirmation. I requested independent validation for H27. H35 is unambiguous and acceptably robust: MSI-high versus non-MSI-high among TP53-intact cells shows an enormous signed WRN dependency difference of +0.780 (interval +0.747 to +0.813), far above the approximate WRN threshold. This refines the accepted H6 MSI-high/WRN association and does not depend on TP53-loss co-occurrence, but it remains a dataset-level association, not causal or generally generalizable. H28 tests whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency is modified by TP53 loss. The signed interaction is near null, +0.008, with a very wide interval (-0.077 to +0.093) and only 81 exposed TP53-loss/CDKN2A-loss cells in the cell-size vector. This is underpowered and cannot adjudicate attenuation; I leave the claim unresolved but closed as a discovery question, and instead registered a simpler follow-up stratum among TP53-loss cells. H29, H30, H31, and H33 were rejected as claims of clinically meaningful stronger dependency in the registered direction because their signed positive upper confidence bounds are below the relevant 10%-scale thresholds, even though some intervals include null or opposite smaller effects. In particular, PIK3CA mutation did not support stronger STAT3 dependency (maximum positive signed effect +0.014, threshold about +0.028), NF1 loss did not support stronger KRAS dependency (maximum positive +0.009, threshold about +0.025), ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger RIT1 dependency (maximum positive +0.023, threshold about +0.026), and MYC amplification under high MYC transcript abundance did not support stronger POLR2A dependency (maximum positive +0.016, threshold about +0.026). These are rejections of the registered positive-direction clinical-scale hypotheses, not proof of no opposite or small effects. H32 and H34 remain unresolved and deferred. KRAS mutation versus BRAF dependency has a signed point of +0.016, below the approximate BRAF threshold of 0.025, with interval -0.001 to +0.034: it does not support acceptance, but a clinically meaningful positive effect cannot be excluded. The SMARCA4-loss-by-ARID1A-loss interaction for SMARCA2 dependency has a positive signed estimate of +0.037, just below the approximate 0.041 threshold, but the interval is wide and crosses zero (-0.015 to +0.089), with only 76 cells in the smallest interaction cell; it is not informative enough to accept or reject. I did not validate H32 or H34 because H27 is the most decision-relevant borderline positive finding. Overall, the evidence continues to support large, specific associations already accepted (MSI-high/WRN, TP53-loss/USP7, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 among TP53-intact cells), while most smaller pathway associations remain null, opposite, or underpowered. None of these conclusions should be read as causal or broadly generalizable.
